sentences.text: The genus Messelornis was formally described by Hesse in 1988.
The type species M. cristata was initially thought to have a comb-like crest, but this feature is now believed to be unrelated plant material.
Specimens of M. cristata show a distinct range of sizes that researchers think is due to sexual dimorphism.
M. nearctica is distinguished from M. cristata by having longer, more slender toes and a unique hypotarsus morphology.
Messelornis is the most abundant bird from the Messel Lagerstätte, with over 500 known specimens representing roughly half of all bird fossils from that site.
One of Messelornis's feathers displayed iridescent coloration, though no chemical analysis has been performed.
Messelornis was probably not an especially adept flier.
Messelornis was an omnivore with a diet that included seeds, fruits, and fish.
Messelornis is classified within the order Gruiformes and is interpreted as a relative of rails.
The parent group of Messelornis is the family Messelornithidae.
The fossil record of Messelornis spans from the Paleocene to the middle Eocene.
Messelornis lived during the Ypresian stage, between 56 and 48.07 million years ago.
The species M. russelli is known from the Paleocene of France and is represented by two poorly preserved humeri.
